title: Zilgit Foils the Villain: Rookie Zoe Edges Philliberto by 1.74 as Sonny's Horse Breaks Loose
dek: A 28-percent underdog took down Team Pillbert, the commissioner hung 146.72 on Randy, and Brucie kept winning while somehow getting less likely to win it all.
body: Every good movie needs a scene where the villain gets got, and Week 7 delivered it. Ghostu-Spider SZN entered Sunday with a 28% pregame win chance against Team Pillbert, and Zoe walked out with an 87.96 to 86.22 win, a margin of 1.74 points. That is roughly one Alan sigh. For a first-year manager, beating the league's resident bad guy in a one-possession game is the kind of win you frame and hang next to the cheese board.

It was not pretty on either side, which made it perfect. Zoe got 1.6 points out of Nico Collins against a 14.01 projection, the week's biggest bust, and still found a way. Philly was hit just as hard, with Jalen Coker posting 1.4 on a 12.57 projection, and in a game decided by less than two points, that is the whole ballgame. Team Pillbert slides to 5-2 and its title odds drop from 26% to 17%, and somewhere Alan is staring at a lineup screen plotting revenge.

The biggest score of the week belonged to the commissioner. The Horse is Hea ran Randy's fumblers off the track 146.72 to 108.52, powered by a three-headed monster: Jaxon Smith-Njigba (26.8 on a 16.25 projection), Jameson Williams (23.6, nearly triple his 8.95 projection) and Bucky Irving (23.5 on 12.81). Sonny's title odds jumped from 11% to 29%, the biggest leap in the league. Randy got a nice 22.12 from Caleb Williams, a rare bit of Bears joy, but Derrick Henry gave him 5.4 against a 17.37 projection and the fumblers are now riding a four-game losing streak.

Habib is back, sort of. Habibsters beat Dawgs 119.84 to 93.58 behind Drake Maye's 27.44, pushing Kaushal to 3-4, a two-game win streak and the fourth playoff spot at 64% odds. The two-time champ is speeding back into the race, though nobody should tell the Georgia highway patrol. The catch: Tony Pollard dropped 35 points on his bench, the week's worst blunder, so he won by 26 while leaving 35 sitting in the garage. Kai, meanwhile, had Tee Higgins score 23.8 on his own bench, which would not have closed the gap but certainly did not help his mood. Dawgs fall to 2-5, and their title odds slide from 5% to 1%.

Then there's Brucie. No Banner only HULK beat JMoney's Counting or not Counting GV 98 to 60.88, moving to 6-1 with a three-game win streak and 100% playoff odds, and he did it with Zay Flowers' 23.7 points on his bench. The man who wasn't sure he even wanted to play is now winning while sitting points. And yet, the strangest number of the week: Ramon's title odds fell from 50% to 38% after a win, because the Horse's explosion made the field scarier. Rage-bait opportunity noted. As for Jordan, Joe Burrow posted the week's best line at 28.88 on a 19.31 projection, and the rest of the lineup managed about 32 combined. The math kid has done the math, and 1-6 with 0% playoff odds is not the answer he wanted.

The waiver wire was busier than a commissioner's inbox. Sonny made seven moves, including dropping Patrick Mahomes for Lamar Jackson, swapping Bryce Young for C.J. Stroud, cutting Terry McLaurin for kicker Will Reichard, flipping Cam Skattebo for Jordan Mason, trading 49ers D/ST for Broncos D/ST, and dropping and re-adding Emanuel Wilson in the same week. Is it abuse of power if it's just extreme clicking? Randy, famously allergic to trades, cleared out Kenny Gainwell, Alec Pierce, Darren Waller, Jordan Addison and the Rams D/ST, adding Jaylin Noel, DeMario Douglas, Cameron Dicker, the Browns D/ST and, of course, the Bears D/ST. He'll release five guys into the wild but never trade one. Elsewhere, Mekhi added Aaron Rodgers, Zoe swapped David Montgomery for Blake Corum, Jordan dropped Ladd McConkey for J.K. Dobbins, Kaushal grabbed Germie Bernard and Tre Tucker, and Ramon upgraded kickers from Eddy Pineiro to Brandon Aubrey, because of course the rich get richer.

Week 8 has a headliner: Team Pillbert vs. The Horse is Hea, two 5-2 teams fighting for the second seed, the villain against the commissioner. Kaushal and Zoe meet in a 3-4 vs. 3-4 game that matters a lot more for the playoff race than the records suggest, especially for Zilgit at 7% playoff odds. Randy tries to snap a four-game skid against Jordan, who is just trying to find a lineup that adds up. And Mekhi gets the unenviable job of facing Brucie, which means the league's football brain is the last best hope of making the league's angriest gamer throw a controller.

social.text: 28% win chance? We don't do math in Wisconsin, we do WINS. 87.96 to 86.22. Zilgit took down Philliberto. Somebody bring the cheese curds.

social.author: Villain Watch
social.text: Team Pillbert loses by 1.74 with Jalen Coker putting up 1.4. The bad guy got foiled by a rookie. Every superhero movie has this scene. Alan will be back, and he'll be meaner.

social.author: Horse Racing Desk
social.text: 146.72. JSN, Jameson Williams, Bucky Irving. The Horse is officially loose. Title odds 11% to 29% in one week. Worst to first was not a fluke.

social.author: Commish Accountability Project
social.text: Sonny made SEVEN roster moves this week, including dropping and re-adding Emanuel Wilson. We're not saying he's abusing the waiver wire. We're saying we'd like to see the logs.

social.author: Brucie Rage Tracker
social.text: Ramon goes to 6-1 and his title odds DROP from 50% to 38%. Somebody please show him this chart while he's mid-game. For science.

social.author: Fumblers Support Group
social.text: Four straight losses. Derrick Henry with 5.4. Randy dropped five guys this week but would rather eat the roster than trade it. At least Caleb gave us 22. Bear down, whatever.

social.author: Dawg Pound Insider
social.text: Sources say Tee Higgins put up 23.8 on the Dawgs bench and Kai responded by picking up Aaron Rodgers. The waiver king has something cooking. Or it's desperation. Possibly both.

social.author: Speed Trap Sports
social.text: Habib wins by 26 with 35 points of Tony Pollard parked on the bench. Two straight wins and sitting in the 4th seed. Clocked doing 90 in a playoff race zone.

social.author: Numbers Don't Lie Pod
social.text: Burrow: 28.88. Rest of JMoney's lineup: about 32. Final: 60.88. Sometimes the numbers lie to you, Jordan.

bios.1: Sonny's defending champs dropped 146.72 on Randy and saw their title odds nearly triple to 29%. At 5-2 with seven waiver moves in a single week, the commissioner is either a genius tinkerer or the most active clicker in league history, and a showdown with Alan looms.
bios.2: Randy is 3-4 and riding a four-game slide after a 146.72 shellacking from Sonny. He cleaned house on waivers, including adding the Bears D/ST, but at 27% playoff odds the fumblers need wins, not just new names.
bios.3: Jordan is 1-6 with 0% playoff odds after a 60.88-point outing that wasted Joe Burrow's week-best 28.88. JMoney swapped Ladd McConkey for J.K. Dobbins and now gets a slumping Randy, a chance to play spoiler and prove the numbers can still add up.
bios.4: Philly's squad is still 5-2 and sitting at 95% playoff odds, but a 1.74-point loss to a rookie dented the villain's aura and dropped his title odds to 17%. Next up is the commissioner, which is either a redemption game or a second straight bad week for the bad guy.
bios.5: Mekhi is 2-5 after a loss to Habibsters, with Tee Higgins scoring 23.8 on the bench and title odds sliding to 1%. The waiver king added Aaron Rodgers, and he'll need every trick he knows against the league-leading HULK next week.
bios.6: Kaushal has won two straight to climb to 3-4 and grab the fourth playoff spot at 64% odds. The two-time champ is speeding back into contention, though leaving 35 Tony Pollard points on the bench suggests the ceiling is even higher.
bios.7: Ramon is 6-1 with a three-game win streak, the league's top scoring total at 927.4, and a locked-up playoff spot. The only crack in the armor is a title-odds dip from 50% to 38% after the Horse's eruption, which is exactly the kind of thing that keeps Brucie up at night.
bios.8: Zoe's rookie season got its signature moment with an upset of Team Pillbert as a 28% underdog. At 3-4 with 7% playoff odds the climb is steep, but a matchup with Kaushal next week gives Zilgit a real shot at shaking up the race.
